literature_claim: ATP13A3 is an endomembrane polyamine transporter whose deficiency causes endothelial polyamine imbalance and is a validated pulmonary arterial hypertension gene.
main_caveats: The displacement call is inferential because the screen lacks pulmonary vascular cells, glia, DNA indel readout, polyamine measurements, and direct protein-level ATP13A3 engagement.
summary: All 22 measured Atp13a3 neuronal cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10; 215 MB Dopa had no Atp13a3 rows and was not tested.
why_it_matters: The null should not be read as global ATP13A3 inertness or failed perturbation. Known ATP13A3 loss-of-function biology concentrates in polyamine transport and pulmonary endothelial dysfunction, whereas this assay sampled sparse NeuN-positive postmitotic brain neurons; any real effect is therefore displaced to vascular/non-neuronal lineages and may be buffered in neurons by parallel polyamine synthesis and uptake systems.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: ATP1A1 and other Na/K-ATPase α isoforms act through pump currents and ion gradients, whereas multiple ATP1A1 diseases are driven by tissue- and allele-specific missense mechanisms.
main_caveats: No DNA indel, protein, pump-current, membrane-voltage, or cell-abundance depletion measurement is available; 217 P MY Pineal Glut has only 26 perturbed nuclei.
summary: Twenty recovered Atp1a1 cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite uniformly negative Atp1a1 self logFC and significant self down-regulation in several large groups.
why_it_matters: Atp1a1 encodes an ion pump whose first phenotypes are membrane voltage and Na+/K+/Ca2+ handling; the absence of UPR, ISR, proteostasis, autophagy, or synaptic-collapse transcripts in the FDR surface is informative for surviving juvenile NeuN+ nuclei, but it is not evidence that α1 loss is physiologically inert. The real effect could remain electrophysiologic, require more complete pump depletion, or require dominant missense/leak alleles rather than simple CRISPR LoF.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Atp1a2 alpha2 is predominantly astrocytic in brain and supports astrocytic K+/glutamate handling; severe ATP1A2/ATP1A3-associated cortical malformations occur in an early developmental disease context.
main_caveats: The small cell counts in several groups reduce power, but the common mechanistic reason for the zeros is the targeted lineage, not the modest self-transcript drop.
summary: Eighteen measured neuronal groups had 0 Atp1a2 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 and flat self-transcripts.
why_it_matters: Because the established alpha2 Na,K-ATPase program is astrocytic K+/glutamate clearance, these neuronal nulls mainly show that the real adult lineage was absent from the NeuN+ screen; rare developmental ATP1A2 cortical-malformation biology would also require a pre-P16 assay.

literature_claim: Loss of alpha2 Na,K-ATPase is expected to act through astrocytic ion and glutamate handling, including GLT-1a-coupled glutamate clearance.
main_caveats: The top FDR values, 0.221-0.333, are not accepted hits and were not expanded into programs.
summary: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 054 CNU-MGE GABA had nominal top genes but 0 accepted downstream Atp1a2 DEGs.
why_it_matters: Treating these near-misses as biology would manufacture a pathway from isolated BH-rejected genes; the same astrocyte-lineage mismatch that explains the strict nulls also explains why weak neuronal ranks do not recover the expected alpha2/glutamate-clearance program.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: ATP1A3 has a prenatal cortical developmental role and alpha3 serves as a neuronal rescue pump after repeated action potentials.
main_caveats: True indel status is unmeasured, but the same design produced a strong 151 response, and several cortical groups showed significant Atp1a3 mRNA self-reduction.
summary: Eight glutamatergic cortical or hippocampal classes had zero downstream Atp1a3 genes at FDR<0.10 despite 46-147 perturbed cells and negative Atp1a3 self-logFC values.
why_it_matters: A fetal cortical malformation program would require perturbing ATP1A3 before P16 neuronal specification, while the alpha3 pump's postnatal rescue role is most stressed by repeated firing rather than by basal snRNA-seq; these zeros therefore should not be read as proof that cortical excitatory neurons do not need Atp1a3.

literature_claim: The ATP1A3 alpha3 isoform restores large Na+ transients after repeated neuronal activity and is enriched in selected early postnatal inhibitory neurons.
main_caveats: Interneuron firing was not measured, so the unseen phenotype may be electrical rather than absent.
summary: 052 Pvalb Gaba and 053 Sst Gaba had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes even with strong Atp1a3 self-reduction.
why_it_matters: ATP1A3 is expected to matter in fast neuronal firing, and human infant cortex shows ATP1A3 persistence in inhibitory neurons including parvalbumin interneurons; the lack of a resting P37-44 nuclear RNA program mainly says that this mosaic perturbation did not push these interneurons into chronic stress.

literature_claim: ATP1A3-related neurological episodes can be precipitated by environmental or physiological stressors, and alpha3 function is recruited after high neuronal Na+ load.
main_caveats: The weak 059 signal is sub-threshold and should not be mined into a pathway.
summary: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and 308 CB GABA had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes; 059 was only weak, with a best downstream FDR of 0.147.
why_it_matters: ATP1A3 disorders are often paroxysmal and triggered by fever, stress, alcohol, exercise, or other load states, so subcortical basal snRNA zeros are poor evidence against a circuit or excitability phenotype that would emerge only under demand.

literature_claim: ATP1A3 pathogenic missense variants cause a broad spectrum that includes paroxysmal neurologic, oculomotor, apnea, autonomic, and fever-induced manifestations, and disease can arise through haploinsufficient or dominant-negative loss of function.
main_caveats: The attribution to under-sampled hindbrain circuitry is inferential from the tissue dissection and clinical anatomy.
summary: 191 MB P MY GABA was weak rather than robust and 217 P MY Pineal Glut was null despite strong Atp1a3 self-reduction.
why_it_matters: Apnea, oculomotor, autonomic, and fever-induced phenotypes in ATP1A3 disease are plausibly circuit-level or in hindbrain/brainstem lineages that were not comprehensively retained in this whole-brain-minus-hindbrain, NeuN-enriched design; a missense-specific dominant-negative mechanism would also not be guaranteed to appear after CRISPR loss of function.

literature_claim: Rapid-onset dystonia-parkinsonism is part of ATP1A3-related disorder, but levodopa response is usually transient or minimal.
main_caveats: n_pert=20 and one sub-threshold event with FDR 0.184 make this weaker than a well-powered null.
summary: 215 MB Dopa had only 20 perturbed nuclei and no downstream FDR<0.10 genes after Atp1a3 perturbation.
why_it_matters: RDP is not a classic dopamine-synthesis deficiency and usually responds minimally to levodopa, so the absence of a cell-autonomous dopaminergic transcriptional program is directionally credible, although the low nucleus count makes it weak evidence only.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Strong SERCA inhibition should deplete ER Ca2+ and trigger a UPR, while this P16 CRISPR screen used a sparse partial genetic perturbation.
main_caveats: DNA indels and ER Ca2+ were not measured; a rare responsive subtype within the broad glutamatergic pools could have been diluted.
summary: 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 after Atp2a2 perturbation.
why_it_matters: For a SERCA pump, the expected detectable phenotype is CHOP/HSPA5/XBP1-type ER stress; that program was seen in other neurons in the same assay but not in these glutamatergic pools. The non-result is therefore best read as failure to cross a cell-type/CRISPR-severity threshold for ER Ca2+ store depletion, not as a limitation of snRNA-seq to capture UPR.

literature_claim: SERCA loss is expected to cause ER Ca2+ stress only after store-refilling capacity falls below the requirement for ER protein folding and calcium signaling.
main_caveats: Target mRNA reduction is not DNA editing; the logFC values do not prove full biallelic loss in every nucleus.
summary: 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut, 052 Pvalb Gaba, and 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA all significantly reduced the Atp2a2 transcript but still had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: These are the cleanest buffered nulls: the target mRNA moved, yet the Hspa5/Creld2/Ddit3/Chac1 program that the same assay detects elsewhere was absent. That argues for cell-type-specific ER-calcium reserve below the transcriptional UPR threshold, while leaving open that stronger SERCA2 loss could still flip the cells into stress.

literature_claim: SERCA blockade can create a UPR, but the response is a thresholded secondary transcriptional outcome of ER Ca2+ store depletion.
main_caveats: The explanation is inferential; stronger or acute pharmacologic SERCA inhibition in the same cell groups could reveal a response.
summary: 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 053 Sst Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut had 31-37 perturbed nuclei and 0 Atp2a2 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: Because Atp2a2 can drive a large UPR in the same experiment, these groups are not negative because the assay lacks stress markers. A SERCA2 UPR would have to be frequent across each broad pooled class to clear FDR here, so their zeros should not be promoted to evidence that SERCA2 is inert in these neuronal classes.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: PMCA1 controls plasma-membrane Ca2+ extrusion; calcium influx can couple to neuronal transcription, and human ATP2B1 variants are associated with neurodevelopmental delay.
main_caveats: This is not proof that DNA editing failed or that these neurons have no Ca2+-handling phenotype; the assay did not measure Ca2+ transients, evoked activity, double-pump loss, vascular lineages, embryonic lineages, or DNA indels.
summary: All 21 recovered non-151 Atp2b1 groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10; 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 145 MH-LH TH Glut were only weak/sub-threshold, with minimum downstream FDR values 0.145, 0.248, and 0.102.
why_it_matters: PMCA1 is expected to change Ca2+ clearance first. Outside the sensitive thalamic state, a single acute P16 Atp2b1 lesion evidently did not drive a basal Fos/Nr4a1/Vgf-like nuclear program; the likely real effects are altered Ca2+ kinetics, challenge-dependent or PMCA/NCX-combinatorial buffering, or earlier developmental roles rather than steady-state snRNA DE at P37-P44.

literature_claim: PMCA2 loss perturbs Purkinje mGluR1-Homer-IP3R1 protein complexes and, after lifelong partial loss, glutamate-receptor transcripts decline only by 8 weeks.
main_caveats: DNA indels and PMCA2 protein were not assayed; the 308 CB GABA aggregate may dilute Purkinje subpopulations.
summary: 308 CB GABA had 104 Atp2b2-perturbed nuclei, a significant on-target Atp2b2 decrease, and 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The expected PMCA2 signal is a Purkinje calcium-flux and synaptic-complex phenotype whose strongest mouse readouts are protein abundance, dendritic morphology, and later glutamate-receptor transcripts; a broad snRNA-seq group after P16 sparse CRISPR can miss that biology even when Atp2b2 RNA is reduced.

literature_claim: The PMCA2-null mGluR1, Homer3, and IP3R1 protein decreases were reported as cerebellum-selective and absent from hippocampus.
main_caveats: The screen did not measure calcium transients or subspine localization of the PMCA2w synaptic pump.
summary: The hippocampal/amygdalar glutamatergic groups 012 and 017 had 84 and 94 Atp2b2-perturbed nuclei, respectively, and each had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: Prior PMCA2-null work found the mGluR1-Homer-IP3R1 protein decrease in cerebellum but not hippocampus, so these zeros argue against a shared hippocampal nuclear-RNA cascade while still leaving local dendritic-spine calcium nanodomain effects untested.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: PMCA2 is a specialized neuronal and hair-cell pump, and Atp2b2/ATP2B2 phenotypes concentrate in hearing, balance, cerebellar, motor, and neurodevelopmental systems rather than predicting a uniform transcriptomic response in every adult brain neuron.
main_caveats: Some cell-type-specific physiology could still appear with electrophysiology, calcium imaging, stronger biallelic editing, or single-subtype Purkinje/motor-neuron sampling.
summary: The remaining cortical, thalamic, hypothalamic, midbrain, dopaminergic and pineal groups carried 29-280 Atp2b2-perturbed nuclei per group and all had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes; 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut had only one subthreshold downstream gene at FDR<0.20.
why_it_matters: The dominant Atp2b2 phenotypes occur in specialized Purkinje, auditory/vestibular, and motor-neuron contexts that are absent, rare, or aggregated in this brain-nucleus taxonomy. The zero surface in these groups is best read as absence of a generalized neuronal PMCA2 stress transcriptome, not strong evidence that PMCA2 calcium extrusion is inert in every sampled neuron.

literature_claim: PMCA3 is enriched at cerebellar parallel-fiber presynaptic terminals and ATP2B3 missense variants impair calcium-pump function in ataxia models.
main_caveats: The dataset does not provide raw PMCA3 protein or calcium measurements for the cerebellar GABA nuclei.
summary: 308 CB GABA had 50 Atp2b3-perturbed nuclei, Atp2b3 logFC -0.155/FDR 1.0, and 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, but it is not the glutamatergic parallel-fiber lineage where PMCA3 is classically enriched.
why_it_matters: The cerebellar disease prior localizes PMCA3 to presynaptic granule-cell parallel fibers; a GABAergic cerebellar aggregate is therefore an off-lineage test and could easily miss the real cerebellar consequence.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: PMCA3 is a local neuronal calcium extruder whose isoform-specific effects can be buffered or revealed by interacting calcium-handling systems.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured, and this null does not exclude acute local Ca2+ dynamics or double-perturbation dependencies.
summary: Twenty non-cerebellar Atp2b3-measured groups had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, including Pvalb, thalamic Prkcd/Grin2c, and MB Glut groups with significant Atp2b3 self-transcript decreases.
why_it_matters: PMCA3 controls local plasma-membrane calcium extrusion; that phenotype is expected to appear first in Ca2+ imaging or electrophysiology, and the absence of the a priori calcium/IEG/UPR RNA programs argues that it did not propagate into a detectable sustained transcriptional state after sparse P16 LoF.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: SPCA1 loss can cause embryonic Golgi/ER stress and neural-tube closure defects, perturb neuronal polarity in culture, and disrupt keratinocyte Ca2+/Mn2+-dependent adhesion and trafficking pathways.
main_caveats: The screen lacks DNA indel sequencing, SPCA1 protein measurement, Golgi Ca2+/Mn2+ readouts, histology, and perturbed-cell abundance estimates.
summary: All 22 measured Atp2c1 cell groups were FDR-null rather than weak responders; the missing 215 MB Dopa group was not tested.
why_it_matters: The zero response is not explained by reading a flat Atp2c1 mRNA row as failed editing. Instead, the literature-predicted SPCA1 phenotypes are concentrated in embryonic morphogenesis, keratinocyte adhesion, Golgi ion flux, glycosylation, and protein trafficking; this screen would have detected a secondary UPR/apoptotic transcriptome and did not see one, so the null is an informative absence of recovered-cell stress but an untrustworthy claim of general Atp2c1 inertness.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Strong ATP6AP2 loss is expected to disrupt V-ATPase-dependent acidification, autophagy and, in early neural cells, Wnt-linked development and survival.
main_caveats: DNA indels, ATP6AP2 protein, lysosomal pH, autophagic flux, and cell abundance were not measured; the stage/threshold attribution is inferential.
summary: Seventeen measured groups had zero Atp6ap2 downstream DE genes at FDR<0.10 despite recurrent negative Atp6ap2 self-transcript estimates.
why_it_matters: The absent Wnt, lysosomal, autophagy, and ER-stress programs are informative because this snRNA-seq assay did recover those types of responses for Ctnnb1/Lrp6 and Rab7. For ATP6AP2 itself, however, the literature places the most catastrophic V-ATPase/Wnt effects in embryonic progenitors or in stronger chronic depletion; a P16 sparse perturbation sampled only specified surviving neurons 3-4 weeks later. These zeros therefore should not be taken as evidence that Atp6ap2 is inert in the listed lineages.

literature_claim: ATP6AP2 deficiency is expected to create V-ATPase/autophagy pathology, not an isolated Uqcr11 transcriptional program.
main_caveats: Only 21 perturbed nuclei were available, but the interpretation rests on lack of FDR<0.10 and lack of recurrence, not on cell count alone.
summary: 217 P MY Pineal Glut was weak rather than positive: only Uqcr11 approached the threshold at FDR=0.145 in 21 Atp6ap2-perturbed nuclei.
why_it_matters: A single sub-threshold mitochondrial respiratory-chain gene was not recurrent with the Atp6v0a1 or Hyou1 effects and is less convincing than a clean zero. The cell group is therefore treated as an unconfirmed tail of the same delayed or buffered V-ATPase biology rather than as a new Atp6ap2 program.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: V-ATPase a1 loss or pathogenic variants are expected to perturb lysosomal acidification, autophagic flux, mTORC1, neuron viability, and synaptic-vesicle filling, with much of the human disease record involving early development or missense alleles rather than acute null alleles in settled neurons.
main_caveats: DNA editing was not assayed; the modest or flat Atp6v0a1 mRNA row is therefore not a standalone failed-KO call, and nominal sub-threshold DE rows were not interpreted as pathway signal.
summary: All 22 measured Atp6v0a1 cell groups, including the eight with FDR<0.10 self-transcript decreases, had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The zero is real on the snRNA axis—expected lysosomal and stress transcripts were also absent—but it should not be read as biological inertness of V0a1. ATP6V0A1 biology lives in organelle and synaptic-vesicle proton handling, mTORC1 phosphorylation, autophagic flux, developmental integrity, and pathogenic missense alleles, any of which can be missed by acute P16 sparse LoF in NeuN+ nuclei harvested only after surviving cells persist for 3-4 weeks.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Severe V-ATPase A-subunit dysfunction should perturb lysosomal pH and downstream stress or autophagy, whereas human ATP6V1A disease is dominated by developmental de novo missense variants with pH-shift phenotypes.
main_caveats: No DNA indel data or edited-cell dropout estimates are available; n_pert was as low as 23 in this group of cell types.
summary: Forebrain excitatory Atp6v1a null or weak groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite recovery of the target transcript and at most a weak L5 ET subthreshold surface.
why_it_matters: Because V-ATPase biology predicts lysosomal or ISR stress that this assay should have detected if chronically engaged, absence in these groups is best explained by buffering below the proton-pump failure threshold plus mismatch between P16 CRISPR LoF and prenatal/early-postnatal dominant missense disease mechanisms, not by forebrain excitatory neurons being irrelevant to Atp6v1a.

literature_claim: Atp6v1a participates in V-ATPase-dependent synaptic vesicle and organelle acidification, and pathogenic ATP6V1A variants can alter lysosomal homeostasis.
main_caveats: The non-transcriptional displacement applies only to vesicle physiology; the absent lysosomal stress program remains informative.
summary: Inhibitory and cerebellar GABA groups were downstream-null, including 052 Pvalb Gaba where Atp6v1a RNA was itself significantly depleted but no other gene reached FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: Fast-spiking or GABAergic neurons could reveal V-ATPase loss through vesicle loading or excitability phenotypes outside snRNA, but a chronic lysosomal failure should still have left ISR/autophagy transcripts; the measured self-transcript-only Pvalb result therefore supports a buffered partial-loss state.

literature_claim: V-ATPase and lysosomal membrane genes can be neurodevelopmental or neurodegenerative disease genes when organelle pH control is sufficiently disrupted.
main_caveats: Edited-cell survival and protein-level V-ATPase activity were not measured.
summary: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, and 155 MB Glut had no Atp6v1a downstream FDR genes, even though 155 MB Glut showed significant target RNA reduction.
why_it_matters: The midbrain target-only RNA hit demonstrates that transcript depletion can be absorbed without a nuclear stress response; the same flatness of Atp6v0a1 and Atp13a2 comparators in matched groups reinforces that juvenile postmitotic glutamatergic neurons did not mount a generic lysosomal-acidification transcriptome.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: V-ATPase disruption is expected to affect lysosomal, endosomal, and synaptic-vesicle acidification, and V-ATPase subunit defects can cause early developmental or neurodevelopmental disease.
main_caveats: Indels, ATP6V1E1 protein depletion, organelle pH, and cell loss were not directly measured; singleton nominal genes in weak groups were deliberately not interpreted as programs.
summary: Seventeen measured Atp6v1e1 cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10, including four groups with only weak sub-threshold islands.
why_it_matters: The missing response is not explained by the flat Atp6v1e1 transcript alone. V-ATPase loss should first change organelle pH, synaptic vesicle loading, or autophagic flux; a secondary TFEB/UPR/ISR RNA program would have been detectable if it were strong, but it was absent. The nulls therefore argue that this P16 sparse LoF did not cross a sustained lysosome-stress threshold in most postmitotic guide-positive neurons, not that ATP6V1E1 is dispensable.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: ATP8A2 loss primarily perturbs phosphatidylserine/phosphatidylethanolamine flipping and produces chronic axonal, sensory, and cerebellar disease phenotypes.
main_caveats: Atp8a2 protein loss and DNA indels were not assayed; individual low-count groups, especially MB Dopa and P MY Pineal Glut, would have limited power for very small RNA effects.
summary: Twenty measured non-effect Atp8a2 cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite being measured with 24-160 perturbed nuclei per group.
why_it_matters: The nulls should not be read as proof that mature Atp8a2 loss is inert: ATP8A2's primary PS/PE-flippase output is a membrane-lipid and axonal-transport phenotype, the strongest animal phenotypes include retina, cochlea, spinal/peripheral axons, and chronic development, and the dataset lacked Atp8a1/Tmem30a combinatorial tests.

literature_claim: ATP8A2 biology predicts phospholipid-asymmetry and axonal or cerebellar phenotypes, not isolated subthreshold single-gene rank tails in L5 extratelencephalic or thalamic nuclei.
main_caveats: Because these groups are closer to the significance boundary than the strict null groups, their no-effect calls are less stable and should not be overinterpreted.
summary: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut and 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut were weak, not positive: each had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 with closest downstream FDRs of 0.173 and 0.187.
why_it_matters: The near-threshold rank tails do not rescue an ATP8A2 program; the same expected stress, axonal, apoptotic, and P4-compensation genes were absent, so these groups remain off-axis weak nulls rather than interpretable L5-ET or thalamic phenotypes.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: ATP9A pathogenic loss causes neurodevelopmental disease and, in null mice or knockdown neurons, abnormal endosomal recycling, reduced neurites and dendritic spines, and altered excitatory synaptic transmission.
main_caveats: The P/MY/pineal group has only 24 perturbed nuclei and no significant self-transcript drop; no DNA indel data are available; this assay cannot see dendritic spines, electrophysiology, cargo localization, or GTPase activation.
summary: Seventeen recovered Atp9a cell groups were strict transcriptional nulls, with 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite negative Atp9a logFC in each group.
why_it_matters: ATP9A loss is expected to perturb endosomal recycling, Rab5/Rab11 activity, neurite architecture, and synaptic transmission; these are local membrane and developmental wiring phenotypes that need not generate a whole-snRNA stress program 3-4 weeks after a sparse P16 knockout. Thus these zeros should not be read as evidence that Atp9a is biologically inert in the neurons.

literature_claim: ATP9A biology predicts a trafficking or synaptic phenotype more directly than a large nuclear transcriptional module.
main_caveats: Weak status is based only on proximity of the lowest adjusted p-values to the FDR threshold; the nominal leading genes were not interpreted as biology.
summary: Three Atp9a groups were weak rather than positive: 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and 191 MB P MY GABA had 0 downstream FDR hits but minimum downstream FDR values of 0.266, 0.439, and 0.172 respectively.
why_it_matters: These subthreshold tails are less trustworthy than the strict zeros as evidence for an Atp9a-regulated program because no individual downstream gene crosses FDR<0.10 and the expected Rab5/Rab11/retromer transcripts remain absent.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Complete Atr loss is embryonic lethal, proliferating neural progenitors require ATR to suppress replication-associated DNA damage, and postmitotic neuronal loss preferentially manifests as presynaptic hyperexcitability without DDR activation.
main_caveats: DNA indel frequencies and ATR protein depletion were not assayed; sparse mosaic perturbation and low per-group Atr cell counts further reduce sensitivity, but they are secondary caveats rather than the gene-specific explanation.
summary: All 21 measured Atr cell groups had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 even though the Atr transcript was directly tested in each group.
why_it_matters: ATR is most transcriptionally consequential in cycling progenitors experiencing endogenous replication stress; this P16 AAV-PHP.eB CRISPR experiment sampled sparse NeuN+ postmitotic neurons after major fate specification and did not assay progenitors. The better-supported postmitotic ATR phenotype is altered firing and presynaptic vesicle handling rather than a p53 or UPR transcriptome, so the observed flat nuclear RNA surface is not reliable evidence that Atr is inert in these neurons.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Atrn loss produces CNS hypomyelination and spongiform/vacuolar pathology, with zitter-rat data implicating macrophage/microglial effects on oligodendrocyte differentiation.
main_caveats: The same explanation is less specific for thalamic groups than for telencephalic myelination contexts; engagement by DNA indels was not measured.
summary: Atrn had no FDR<0.10 downstream genes in 15 cortical, hippocampal, striatal, GABAergic, and thalamic groups, even though 005, 022, and 151 had the weakest subthreshold surfaces and 054/151 had FDR-significant Atrn self-depletion.
why_it_matters: The classic Atrn phenotype is myelination/spongiform disease with oligodendrocyte and macrophage/microglial involvement; those lineages were under-sampled in a NeuN+ neuronal screen, and acute P16 editing does not recreate the germline early-postnatal inflammatory and myelination context. These zeros therefore displace the expected biology rather than proving Atrn inertness in cortex, hippocampus, striatum, or thalamus.

literature_claim: Atrn functions in agouti/Agrp melanocortin signaling, and Atrn mRNA is present in rat hypothalamic nuclei including arcuate-region anatomy.
main_caveats: The screen still perturbed broad HY neuronal nuclei after P16, so a large cell-autonomous hypothalamic transcriptome would have been visible; the null is untrustworthy only for the rare melanocortin trafficking phenotype.
summary: Atrn was also flat in the two broad hypothalamic groups, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, and Agrp/Mc1r/Mc2r perturbations had no FDR<0.10 downstream genes across Atrn-matched groups.
why_it_matters: For melanocortin biology, the expected effect is ligand/receptor trafficking and cAMP modulation in rare Agrp/POMC/MC4R cells. A broad snRNA-seq neuronal class with no MC4R perturbation target represented is poorly aligned to that effect, and protein trafficking need not yield a secondary stress program if the rare circuit was not captured.

literature_claim: Attractin-deficient zitter rats develop activated microglial clusters and age-dependent dopaminergic cell death in the substantia nigra.
main_caveats: 155 had a subthreshold best downstream FDR of 0.211, but no robust FDR<0.10 DEG; the exact 215 MB Dopa Atrn surface is missing rather than negative.
summary: 155 MB Glut was only weak and 191 MB P MY GABA was null after Atrn perturbation, while the dedicated 215 MB Dopa group was not recovered for Atrn.
why_it_matters: Zitter-rat midbrain degeneration is centered on substantia-nigra dopaminergic neurons with activated microglial clusters. This Atrn screen did not recover the dopaminergic group and largely excluded microglia, so the glutamatergic and GABAergic midbrain zeros do not test the literature-predicted DA/microglia lesion.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Embryonic Atrx deletion in forebrain/neural progenitors causes neocortical and hippocampal hypocellularity through neuronal death.
main_caveats: DNA editing and pre-capture death were not measured.
summary: Seven cortical/hippocampal excitatory groups had 0 downstream Atrx genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: P16 CRISPR occurred after the embryonic corticogenesis window in which Atrx loss causes p53-linked neuronal death, so these zeros do not show that ATRX is developmentally inert in forebrain neurons.

literature_claim: ATRX biology includes early neural progenitors, retinal interneurons, and unresolved glial contributions in contexts outside the sampled inhibitory nuclei.
main_caveats: Small subtype effects could be averaged within broad cell groups.
summary: Seven inhibitory or cerebellar groups were null or weak, including the isolated subthreshold Pvalb Fam229b signal.
why_it_matters: The weak Pvalb nominal hit should not be promoted to pathway biology, and the known ATRX-sensitive interneuron/glial contexts are not these sampled postnatal NeuN+ inhibitory groups.

literature_claim: Current ATRX neurodevelopmental reviews do not predict a specific MH-LH/TH glutamatergic dependency.
main_caveats: Only 29 perturbed nuclei were available.
summary: 145 MH-LH TH Glut had 0 downstream Atrx genes at FDR<0.10 even though 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut responded.
why_it_matters: This low-confidence terminal null refines the thalamic Atrx response to 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut rather than all nearby thalamic/hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: ATXN1/ATXN1L-CIC activity is required for normal brain development and forebrain cortical maturation, but ATXN1L can stabilize CIC and buffer single Atxn1 loss.
main_caveats: Atxn1L was not itself perturbed and DNA indels were not measured; the buffering explanation is inferred from related genetics.
summary: Seven cortical/telencephalic neuronal groups had no Atxn1 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite being contexts where developmental CIC-family biology might have suggested a response.
why_it_matters: The relevant prior is embryonic or early postnatal forebrain disruption of the ATXN1/ATXN1L-CIC complex, not P16 single Atxn1 loss. The zeros therefore show that acute Atxn1 alone is insufficient in these postmitotic cells; they do not rule out earlier or combined Atxn1/Atxn1l/Cic dependence.

literature_claim: Germline Sca1/Atxn1-null mice show decreased hippocampal CA1 paired-pulse facilitation while long-term and post-tetanic potentiation are normal.
main_caveats: The dataset groups pool several limbic excitatory populations and do not directly record synaptic physiology.
summary: The hippocampal-containing 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut and 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut groups had 75 and 85 perturbed cells, flat Atxn1 self-transcripts, and 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: Atxn1-null mice have a CA1 paired-pulse facilitation phenotype, a synaptic physiology deficit that need not create a large steady-state nuclear RNA program 3-4 weeks after sparse P16 editing. Because the 151-TH group shows that secondary transcription is detectable when present, the hippocampal zero specifically argues that this known hippocampal LoF phenotype is displaced onto physiology rather than being a robust cell-autonomous transcriptomic state here.

literature_claim: CIC-family regulation can affect many lineages, but the Atxn1-Bace1 and developmental forebrain programs do not imply a strong single-Atxn1 LoF response in every mature neuronal class.
main_caveats: This is weakest for 215 MB Dopa and 217 P MY Pineal Glut because only 22 and 28 perturbed cells were recovered.
summary: Ten inhibitory, hypothalamic, midbrain, dopaminergic, pineal and cerebellar-adjacent noncanonical groups outside the forebrain/hippocampal/SCA1 priors had 0 Atxn1 FDR<0.10 downstream genes.
why_it_matters: The assay can see an Atxn1-CIC/Bace1 transcriptional response in 151 TH, but these groups did not mount that secondary program. With no strong literature expectation for single Atxn1 loss in these sampled neuronal states, the parsimonious reading is a genuine negative for acute juvenile Atxn1 LoF, weakened in the smallest 22- and 28-cell groups.

literature_claim: Polyglutamine-expanded ATXN1 drives SCA1 through toxic ATXN1-CIC gain of function, whereas Atxn1-null mice are viable and show no evidence of ataxia or neurodegeneration.
main_caveats: The screen does not isolate aged Purkinje cells and does not introduce an expanded polyglutamine allele.
summary: 308 CB GABA, the only cerebellar GABA class in the 23-group taxonomy, had 72 Atxn1-perturbed cells, Atxn1 logFC -0.101 with FDR 1, and 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: A missing cerebellar transcriptional response after acute wild-type Atxn1 loss should not be read as absence of SCA1 biology. SCA1 polyglutamine toxicity is mediated by a mutant ATXN1-CIC gain-of-function mechanism and Atxn1-null mice do not develop ataxic Purkinje degeneration, so the disease-relevant perturbation is allele-specific and may lie outside this broad CB GABA snRNA-seq group.

literature_claim: SCA10 is driven by an intronic ATTCT expansion and expanded AUUCU repeat RNA rather than by simple Atxn10 coding null.
main_caveats: 308 CB GABA is not a purified adult Purkinje model, and cell loss was not assayed.
summary: 308 CB GABA had no Atxn10 downstream DEG despite 54 perturbed cells, Atxn10 self logFC -0.502, and best downstream FDR 0.855.
why_it_matters: The SCA10 prior is an expanded intronic repeat that makes toxic AUUCU RNA; coding CRISPR loss at P16 removes that allele class, so this zero is not trustworthy evidence that the SCA10 mutation itself would be silent.

literature_claim: Pvalb interneurons are a fast-spiking, stress-vulnerable GABAergic class.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured; 053 has only 41 perturbed cells, and 059 is weak rather than cleanly null.
summary: 046 CTX-CGE GABA, 053 Sst Gaba, 054 CNU-MGE GABA, and 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA lacked downstream Atxn10 genes at FDR<0.10; 054 had clear Atxn10 transcript decrease but no downstream response, and 059 had only one subthreshold feature at FDR 0.220.
why_it_matters: Because 052 Pvalb Gaba mounted a 238-gene ISR/synaptic response, the absence of that program in other GABA classes is a GABA-subclass restriction rather than a readout failure.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: ATXN10 has described neuritogenesis and cytokinesis functions, and whole-animal lethality maps strongly to embryonic and epithelial contexts.
main_caveats: Groups with 40-66 perturbed cells could still miss a tiny one- or two-gene echo.
summary: 001 L5-6 IT Glut, 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut, 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut, 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut, 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut, 022 L5 ET CTX Glut, and 027 NP-CT-L6b-OB Glut had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: ATXN10 neuritogenesis/cytokinesis priors predict morphology, growth-factor, or mitotic programs more than an obligate transcriptional collapse in already specified forebrain projection neurons; weak IT effects show the assay could detect a cortical echo when present.

literature_claim: Existing Atxn10 loss-of-function data do not predict a uniform postnatal diencephalic transcriptional program.
main_caveats: 217 had only 30 perturbed cells and is the weakest null in this set.
summary: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut, 145 MH-LH TH Glut, and 217 P MY Pineal Glut had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes, contrasting with 73 downstream genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
why_it_matters: The thalamic effect was not generic; it was concentrated in the Prkcd/Grin2c glutamatergic class, so the nearby glutamatergic zeros report cell-subclass gating of the perturbation.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
literature_claim: ATXN2 acts in stress-granule/RNA metabolism, expanded ATXN2 alleles modify ALS/SCA2 biology, Atxn2 reduction is protective in TDP-43 mice, and the ATXN2L paralog has overlapping RNA-granule functions.
main_caveats: This null is untrustworthy for polyQ-expanded ATXN2, TDP-43-challenged neurons, ATXN2/ATXN2L double loss, non-neuronal cells, or aged tissue; it is informative for the acute unchallenged single-gene LoF axis assayed here.
summary: Eighteen measured non-151 cell groups had zero Atxn2 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: The zeros are not readout failure: the same assay detected broad signatures for Tardbp, Matr3, Zbtb7a, Yy1 and Psmb4 in matched neuronal classes. They are also not proof that ATXN2 biology is absent; the best explanation is that acute single-gene loss of wild-type Atxn2 at P16 is buffered in these neurons, while the strongest disease mechanisms require ATXN2 polyglutamine alleles or a TDP-43 stress background and may be further masked by ATXN2L-family compensation.

cell_types: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: ATXN2 and ATXN2L are RNA-granule proteins linked to stress granules, P-bodies and autophagy-related regulation, but a single Gabarapl1 or respiratory-chain near hit is not that program.
main_caveats: The FDRs were 0.1916 and 0.1550, respectively; these weak groups should not be mined for biology unless replicated or strengthened by other evidence.
summary: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and 054 CNU-MGE GABA had only one subthreshold downstream hit each and no FDR<0.10 Atxn2 response.
why_it_matters: The near hits, Gabarapl1 in 009 and Uqcrfs1 in 054, did not recur across groups and did not assemble into the RNA-processing, synaptic, stress-granule, ISR/UPR or autophagy programs expected from ATXN2 biology, so they are weaker evidence than the complete zeros.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Canonical Atxn7 loss affects the SAGA DUB and HAT system and has photoreceptor or cerebellar developmental effects in non-mouse vertebrate and fly systems, whereas SCA7 disease is driven by a polyglutamine allele.
main_caveats: This is a transcriptomic null, not an indel-sequencing or chromatin-assay null; it is strongest for this acute wild-type LoF context and should not be extrapolated to expanded ATXN7.
summary: Nineteen non-cerebellar measured groups had no Atxn7 downstream FDR<0.10 genes; the only weak group was 054 CNU-MGE GABA, whose minimum downstream FDR remained 0.246.
why_it_matters: If wild-type Atxn7 disruption directly destabilized SAGA-driven transcription in these mature neurons, this snRNA-seq design should have detected at least a secondary stress, chromatin-compensation, proteostasis, or synaptic program; none appeared, while Atxn1, Atxn10, Htt, and Atxn2 produced detectable DE in matched groups.

literature_claim: SCA7 and Atxn7 loss-of-function literature centers on photoreceptors, Purkinje-lineage development, and neuron-glia interactions rather than an acute wild-type LoF transcriptome in 38 juvenile cerebellar GABA nuclei.
main_caveats: The group aggregates cerebellar GABA neurons, does not isolate Purkinje cells, and is near the lower end of Atxn7 cell counts.
summary: The cerebellar 308 CB GABA group had 38 Atxn7-perturbed nuclei, Atxn7 logFC 0.056 with FDR 1.0, and zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: This zero should not be read as absence of SCA7-relevant cerebellar biology: the disease allele is a toxic polyglutamine expansion, retinal cells and Bergmann glia were missing from the NeuN+ brain sample, and Atxn7 developmental requirements for photoreceptor and Purkinje programs precede the P16 perturbation used here.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: AUH deficiency is a mitochondrial leucine-catabolic and mitochondrial-protein-synthesis disorder whose direct outputs are metabolites and oxidative phosphorylation rather than obligatory nuclear RNA changes.
main_caveats: The explanation is inferential because the experiment did not measure indels, AUH enzyme activity, organic acids, mitochondrial translation, respiration, or glial/systemic tissues.
summary: Every recovered Auh neuronal cell group had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10; the null most likely reflects AUH biology living on metabolite, mitochondrial-translation, respiration, and systemic or non-neuronal axes that this sparse NeuN+ snRNA assay did not directly measure.
why_it_matters: The null should not be read as a failed perturbation or as evidence that AUH is inert. The assay would have detected a strong secondary nuclear stress response, and none appeared, but the canonical AUH lesion is a mitochondrial leucine-catabolic block rather than a transcription-factor-like program.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Auts2 has documented developmental functions in neocortex, hippocampus, dentate gyrus, neuronal migration, neuritogenesis, and synaptic structure.
main_caveats: Adult or stronger isoform-complete deletion could reveal structural or electrophysiological phenotypes without a large snRNA signature.
summary: Auts2 had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in nine cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic groups, including the weak 007 and 022 groups whose minima were still FDR 0.253 and 0.532.
why_it_matters: The strongest AUTS2 priors in these lineages concern embryonic corticogenesis, dentate development, migration, neurite extension, and synapse morphology; a P16 postmitotic nuclear-RNA screen can easily miss those effects.

literature_claim: AUTS2 expression and model phenotypes are concentrated in developmental cortical, hippocampal, cerebellar, and selected thalamic contexts rather than defining a known postmitotic interneuron transcription factor program.
main_caveats: Sst and CNU-MGE each had sub-threshold adjusted minima, so their zeros should not be over-interpreted as absence of all biology.
summary: Auts2 had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in CTX-CGE, Pvalb, Sst, CNU-MGE, and CNU-LGE/LSX GABA groups.
why_it_matters: The canonical AUTS2 literature does not predict a strong autonomous P16 transcriptional response in already specified telencephalic inhibitory neurons, so the absence of robust DE is a defensible within-assay negative result.

literature_claim: Auts2 is reported in embryonic dorsal thalamus and selected P21 thalamic nuclei, but the established model phenotypes focus on cortex, dentate gyrus, cerebellum, and synapses.
main_caveats: The 217 P MY Pineal Glut bin had only 30 perturbed nuclei, making that component the least secure.
summary: Auts2 had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in CNU-HYa/HY GABA, CNU-HYa/HY/MM Glut, MH-LH-TH Glut, MB Glut, MB/P/MY GABA, and P/MY/Pineal Glut.
why_it_matters: Because the literature gives selective rather than pan-subcortical postnatal AUTS2 expectations, these bins provide weak evidence that Auts2 is transcriptionally inert in this P16-P37 NeuN+ setting outside 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.

literature_claim: Postnatal mouse cerebellum contains high AUTS2 in Purkinje and Golgi neurons, Auts2 cerebellar deletion impairs Purkinje maturation and Cacna1a-linked synapse development, and Purkinje cells are a NeuN-negative neuronal exception.
main_caveats: The dataset does contain a broad CB GABA bin, so Purkinje loss is inferred from NeuN enrichment and known NeuN marker biology rather than from direct cell-identity counts in the parquet.
summary: Auts2 had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in 308 CB GABA despite the known postnatal cerebellar Auts2/Purkinje program; Cacna1a, Grid2, and Pcp2 were all FDR 1.000.
why_it_matters: The expected cerebellar effect lives largely in Purkinje maturation and synapse organization, while Purkinje cells are a NeuN-negative exception and the screen enriched NeuN+ nuclei, so this CB GABA zero is survivor/capture-context limited rather than strong evidence against cerebellar AUTS2 biology.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: AVPR1A acts through rapid GPCR calcium signaling in discrete social-behavior circuits rather than through a known constitutive transcriptional program in every excitatory or inhibitory neuron class.
main_caveats: Null attribution is inferential because DNA indels, receptor protein, peptide release, and behavior were not measured; weak near-miss genes are deliberately not interpreted as programs.
summary: Fifteen cortical, hippocampal, striatal/interneuron, and cerebellar groups had no FDR<0.10 Avpr1a response; the two nominal interneuron near-misses, Grin2d in 046 and Rictor in 053, stayed at FDR 0.465 and 0.284.
why_it_matters: V1a is a peptide-evoked GPCR with regionally sparse circuit roles; without a defined vasopressin/social/water-stress state, and after averaging broad cell classes, a basal snRNA zero is weak evidence that the receptor is inert in the underlying neurons.

literature_claim: Brain vasopressin/oxytocin systems are region- and receptor-specific modulators of social behavior whose principal receptor action is GPCR second-messenger signaling.
main_caveats: These are broad cell-group labels, not named AVPR1A-positive nuclei; no ligand challenge or social-state readout was collected.
summary: Six hypothalamic, thalamic, midbrain, and pontine/medullary groups were also null or weak despite stronger a priori relevance for neuropeptide signaling; 066, 145, 151, and 217 had 0 downstream FDR genes, while 155 and 191 had only Dcaf13 and Spg7 sub-threshold near-misses at FDR 0.252 and 0.411.
why_it_matters: The adjacent 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut Srsf6 event shows that this target was not globally silent, so the remaining subcortical zeros most likely reflect nucleus/state specificity and fast GPCR physiology rather than a reliable absence of AVPR1A biology.

literature_claim: Mouse Avpr1b is concentrated in hippocampal CA2 with lower PVN and amygdala expression, and CA2 Avpr1b supports attack behavior and evoked NMDA/CaMKII-dependent synaptic potentiation.
main_caveats: CA2, PVN, and amygdala receptor-positive nuclei were not isolated as fine subclasses; engagement was not measured by DNA indel sequencing.
summary: The closest limbic and hypothalamic broad groups had 58, 62, 71, and 64 Avpr1b-perturbed nuclei and 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: These zeros do not rule out the established CA2/PVN/amygdala biology: the receptor is sparse within the broad groups sampled here and its main central readouts are AVP/social-stimulus-gated calcium and synaptic effects rather than a tonic RNA program.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: More specific in situ data placed the strongest mouse Avpr1b expression in hippocampal CA2 with only lower expression in PVN and amygdala, rather than widespread high expression across these neuron classes.
main_caveats: This is a group-level baseline negative; single rare receptor-positive cells within a broad class could be diluted below Wilcoxon detection.
summary: The remaining cortical, striatal, thalamic, midbrain, dopaminergic, pontine/pineal, and cerebellar groups also had 0 Avpr1b downstream genes at FDR<0.10; 022 L5 ET CTX Glut was only weak, with best downstream FDR 0.102539.
why_it_matters: Specific mouse mapping does not predict a major Avpr1b-autonomous program in these broad neuron classes, so their flat surfaces are credible negatives for basal postmitotic neuronal RNA even though they say little about pituitary corticotrophs, olfactory bulb, or rare CA2/PVN cells.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Axl and Mertk regulate microglial apoptotic-cell clearance and TAM signaling can control innate SOCS feedback, synaptic pruning, neural-stem-cell survival, and neurotrophin expression outside this sparse postmitotic-neuron context.
main_caveats: The null should not be generalized to non-neuronal CNS cells, retinal pigment epithelium, inflammatory lesions, or TAM-family compound knockouts; Axl protein loss was not assayed by indel sequencing or protein capture.
summary: All 22 recovered Axl cell groups were weak/FDR-null: each had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite 34-198 perturbed nuclei per group and all had Axl self-transcript FDR=1.00.
why_it_matters: The flat result is best explained by the biology of Axl rather than by the expected weak self-transcript: canonical TAM effects usually require Mer/Axl/Tyro3 signaling in phagocytes or neural progenitors, phosphatidylserine-bearing targets, and often inflammatory or double/triple-KO contexts that this P16 sparse NeuN+ assay did not sample.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: B3GAT3 acts in proteoglycan linker biosynthesis, patient fibroblasts show reduced DS/CS/HS proteoglycans, and the described developmental phenotypes lie largely in skeletal, connective, and cardiac systems with HS biology also acting during neural circuit development.
main_caveats: Null attribution is inferential because DNA indels, B3GAT3 protein, HS/CS chain abundance, and perturbed-cell abundance effects were not assayed.
summary: Twenty-two measured B3gat3 cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite B3gat3 transcript detection, with n_pert spanning 23-217 and on-target FDR=1.0 throughout.
why_it_matters: B3GAT3 loss is expected to damage a Golgi-built extracellular glycan linker and developmental proteoglycan signaling, not necessarily to reprogram the nucleus of a sparse postmitotic neuron within 3-4 weeks. The nulls therefore rule out a broad secondary UPR/ISR/GAG-compensation transcriptome in these survivors, but not loss of HS/CS chains, altered synapses, embryonic wiring defects, or connective-tissue/cardiovascular mechanisms.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Published B9d1 biology emphasizes embryonic Hedgehog patterning and ciliary transition-zone membrane gating whose primary effects need not become nuclear RNA changes in postmitotic neurons.
main_caveats: DNA indel formation is unmeasured; the 001 L5-6 IT Glut null has only 20 perturbed nuclei, although several other null groups had substantially larger n.
summary: B9d1 had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every recovered non-CB group, with n_pert from 20 to 180 and self-transcript FDR=1.0 throughout.
why_it_matters: The zeroes do not show that B9d1 is biologically inert; its canonical functions are embryonic patterning and local ciliary transition-zone gating, whereas this assay perturbed sparse postmitotic NeuN+ neurons at P16 and measured nuclear RNA 3-4 weeks later.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: Bach2 controls immune differentiation and was reported in embryonic differentiating neural cells through Maf/AP-1/oxidative-stress-responsive regulatory logic.
main_caveats: DNA indels were not measured; rare classes with 32-58 perturbed cells are less powered, but the absence of an ARE/stress program that snRNA-seq could detect argues against a simple readout failure.
summary: Nineteen Bach2-measured neuronal groups had no downstream FDR<0.10 genes and a Bach2 self-transcript FDR of 1.0.
why_it_matters: Bach2's strongest priors live in B/T immune differentiation and in E12.5 differentiating neuronal or lens cells; a P16 mosaic perturbation assayed only in NeuN+ juvenile neurons is after neuronal fate specification and omits the immune lineages where BACH2 loss is dosage-sensitive. The zeros therefore localize the active biology away from this sampled postmitotic neuronal axis rather than proving Bach2 is globally inert.

literature_claim: Bach2's best-described functions are lineage- and stage-restricted rather than a known mature L2/3 cortical Rnps1 program.
main_caveats: Only 53 perturbed L2/3 nuclei were recovered, and the only nominated downstream gene missed the FDR<0.10 threshold.
summary: 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut showed no FDR<0.10 downstream genes; its best nominal hit was Rnps1 at FDR 0.114.
why_it_matters: The near-threshold Rnps1 result is not enough to construct a program, and the same Bach2 developmental/immune context mismatch that explains the strict nulls also makes this weak L2/3 result unreliable as evidence for a stable postnatal Bach2 function.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: IRSp53 is enriched at excitatory PSDs, interacts with PSD-95/Shank, regulates actin-rich dendritic spines, and deletion alters excitatory synaptic transmission in cortex and hippocampus.
main_caveats: CRISPR engagement was inferred from guide assignment and self-transcript trends rather than indel or protein data; morphology and electrophysiology were not measured.
summary: Telencephalic glutamatergic Baiap2 perturbations had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in nine assayed cortical, hippocampal, and related glutamatergic groups despite generally negative Baiap2 self logFC.
why_it_matters: These are the cell classes nearest the published cortical and hippocampal IRSp53 phenotypes, but the expected phenotype is spine actin, PSD organization, NMDAR/EPSP balance, and behavior rather than an autonomous nuclear RNA program; their nulls should not be used as evidence that Baiap2 is inert at synapses.

literature_claim: IRSp53 is primarily detected in cortical Vglut1/2-positive cells and Viaat-Cre deletion in male mice minimally affects social interaction and hyperactivity compared with Emx1-Cre deletion.
main_caveats: The literature result is behavioral and mPFC-focused; several assayed GABA classes are subcortical, and female Viaat-lineage consequences were not exhaustively excluded.
summary: GABAergic Baiap2 perturbations had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes in CTX-CGE, Pvalb, Sst, CNU-MGE, CNU-LGE, hypothalamic, midbrain/pons/medulla, and cerebellar GABA groups.
why_it_matters: Published cell-type genetics places the strongest Baiap2 requirement in Emx1-lineage glutamatergic neurons and reports minimal male social/locomotor effects after Viaat-lineage deletion; the GABA nuclear null is therefore more credible than the excitatory synaptic null.

literature_claim: Adult BAIAP2/IRSp53 rescue studies and reviews emphasize excitatory synaptic physiology, with mechanistic analyses concentrated in cortex, hippocampus, and mPFC.
main_caveats: 215 MB Dopa and 217 P MY Pineal Glut had only 20 and 22 perturbed cells, respectively; other subcortical groups were better sampled but still assayed only by snRNA-seq.
summary: Subcortical glutamatergic, midbrain glutamatergic, dopaminergic, and pineal/brainstem glutamatergic classes also had 0 Baiap2 downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: The strongest prior for Baiap2 concerns excitatory PSD microstructure in cortical and hippocampal synapses; in these less canonical groups, the CRISPR-snRNA null mainly says that no large cell-autonomous nuclear program was triggered, not that local synapses or circuit physiology would be unchanged.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: BAP1/PR-DUB has strong embryonic, prenatal neuronal, and cancer-lineage functions, with mouse germline loss causing embryonic lethality and fetal enteric loss causing postnatal neuron defects.
main_caveats: Several low-count cortical and hippocampal groups could gain weak hits with more cells; 022 L5 ET should be treated with extra skepticism because its best downstream gene did not pass FDR<0.10.
summary: Telencephalic glutamatergic neurons were robustly null or only weak after P16 Bap1 perturbation: 001, 005, 007, 008, 009, 012, 017, and 027 had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, while 022 had only subthreshold Brd9 at FDR 0.221.
why_it_matters: The informative expectation for BAP1 is prenatal or proliferative chromatin control; this screen hit already specified postmitotic excitatory neurons and excluded the cancer lineages in which BAP1 LoF is strongly penetrant, so these zeros should not be read as developmental inactivity of BAP1.

literature_claim: SCG2 marks the regulated secretory pathway in neuronal and neuroendocrine cells, but the literature does not predict that BAP1 loss should change it in all inhibitory neurons.
main_caveats: Some non-Pvalb inhibitory groups had 24-42 perturbed cells, so a small same-direction signature could have been missed.
summary: All measured inhibitory groups except 052 Pvalb Gaba had 0 Bap1 downstream FDR<0.10 genes.
why_it_matters: The Pvalb Scg2/Rab34/Nomo1 signature shows that inhibitory neurons can respond in this assay, so the Sst, CGE, CNU, MB, and cerebellar inhibitory nulls localize the BAP1-dependent secretory response to a narrower Pvalb chromatin or activity state.

literature_claim: BAP1/PR-DUB is a chromatin complex rather than a pathway with predefined hypothalamic or thalamic subtype specificity.
main_caveats: The assignment of a permissive TH-Prkcd/Grin2c state is inferential because the screen did not measure BAP1 chromatin occupancy or H2AK119ub1.
summary: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 145 MH-LH TH Glut had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes even though 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut had the largest Bap1 response.
why_it_matters: The null is not explained by a general thalamic or hypothalamic readout mismatch; the real BAP1 response is displaced into a specific TH-Prkcd/Grin2c transcriptional state represented by Scg2, Cnot9, Coro6, and Serpine2 changes.

cell_types: 008 L2-3 IT ENT PPP RSP Glut
009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut
literature_claim: BAZ1B haploinsufficiency disrupts Wnt/neurogenic programs in neural progenitors and BAZ1B dosage regulates neural-crest developmental programs.
main_caveats: A stronger or embryonic CNS perturbation could reveal effects; 001, 007, 012 and related small-n groups are weakly powered and were not interpreted through nominal genes.
summary: Telencephalic cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic groups had zero downstream Baz1b FDR<0.10 genes despite measured Baz1b rows.
why_it_matters: BAZ1B's strongest neural prior is regulation of neural-progenitor Wnt signaling and neurogenic commitment; those programs execute before the P16 postmitotic AAV window, so these zeros mainly report a missed developmental window rather than absence of embryonic Baz1b function.

literature_claim: BAZ1B belongs to chromatin-remodeling and DNA-damage complexes and contributes to neural-crest and postnatal organismal developmental phenotypes.
main_caveats: The screen did not measure peripheral neural-crest derivatives, glia, vasculature, cell depletion, H2AX phosphorylation or Pol I/III transcription.
summary: CGE, MGE, striatal/hypothalamic GABA, midbrain, thalamic-neighbor, pineal and cerebellar Baz1b groups lacked downstream FDR<0.10 responses.
why_it_matters: Whole-animal Baz1b phenotypes and BAZ1B neural-crest functions point to embryonic, neural-crest-derived or peripheral visceral tissues that are not represented in this NeuN+ CNS screen; the absent p53/ISR/heat-shock markers make the null informative for surviving P37 neuronal nuclei but not for those displaced compartments.

A one-gene subthreshold Ptprn change in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut is therefore less convincing than the complete absence of FDR<0.10 genes.

summary: Camsap1 was FDR-null in cortical, hippocampal, and cortical GABA groups despite being included in the DE test for each group.
why_it_matters: Published CAMSAP1 biology predicts defects in neurite outgrowth, axon selection, neuronal migration, and cortical lamination; P16 CRISPR in already postmitotic neurons can miss those earlier morphogenetic endpoints, and snRNA-seq can miss direct changes in microtubule-minus-end organization. The absence of any FDR<0.10 stress or apoptosis genes nevertheless shows that these surviving neurons did not mount a robust secondary RNA program.

literature_claim: CAMSAP1 loss is linked to developmental brain malformations and seizures, not to a defined late marker program in each terminal subcortical neuron class sampled here.
main_caveats: The broad groups may dilute rarer vulnerable neurons; 215 MB Dopa and 217 P MY Pineal Glut were not tested for Camsap1.
summary: Camsap1 was also FDR-null in CNU, hypothalamic, thalamic, midbrain/brainstem, and cerebellar neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: Human CAMSAP1 loss involves basal ganglia, hippocampal, midbrain and cerebellar malformations, but those are construction-time phenotypes; the assayed groups are broad P16-perturbed NeuN+ terminal populations. The null is therefore a weak inertness claim rather than proof that Camsap1 never acts in these regions.

literature_claim: CAMTA1 has recognized hippocampal and memory biology, so limbic/entorhinal excitatory neurons were not a priori irrelevant.
main_caveats: Attribution to engagement threshold is inferential; no indel data are available and the nominal genes are not FDR-significant in these two groups.
summary: 009 L2-3 IT PIR AON ENT Glut and 012 MEA LA CA1 DG Glut had 0 FDR<0.10 downstream genes but retained a nominal negative Snhg11 signal as their top gene.
why_it_matters: These are weak, not clean, nulls: given that Snhg11 was significant in every Camta1 responder, the repeated subthreshold Snhg11 shift argues that the same low-level Camta1 core was present but too small to survive whole-transcriptome correction.

literature_claim: CAMTA1 was implicated in human episodic memory and acute adult hippocampal CAMTA1 knockdown impaired long-term memory with synaptic/excitability gene effects.
main_caveats: The dataset pooled CA3, CA2, fasciola cinerea and dentate-gyrus glutamatergic neurons; a CA1-specific or activated-ensemble effect could be diluted.
summary: 017 CA3 CA2-FC DG Glut was a complete Camta1 null with 64 perturbed cells, Camta1 self logFC +0.040 FDR 1.0, and no downstream gene with FDR<1.0.
why_it_matters: The adult CAMTA1 hippocampal literature predicts plasticity and excitability phenotypes, but this P16 CRISPR screen measured unstimulated basal nuclei rather than a memory-encoding or activity-evoked state; Camta1 loss may need that activity context to become transcriptionally visible in CA3/CA2/DG neurons.

literature_claim: CAMTA1 is broadly implicated in the nervous system, but prior literature does not establish a specific basal CGE-interneuron requirement.
main_caveats: The mechanism for CGE buffering is not directly measured; only subthreshold Snrpn and Snhg11 point toward a weak core response.
summary: 046 CTX-CGE GABA had 76 Camta1-perturbed cells and 0 FDR<0.10 downstream genes; Snrpn was its best row but stopped at FDR 0.156.
why_it_matters: Camta1 strongly affected Pvalb and weaker MGE-derived GABAergic groups, so the CGE zero is a lineage-specific attenuation of the same program rather than evidence that inhibitory neurons as a class ignore Camta1.

literature_claim: CAMTA1 is a broad nervous-system gene but no literature predicts a strong postnatal basal CNU-LGE LSX GABA transcriptome after Camta1 loss.
main_caveats: A stimulated, embryonic, or stronger biallelic deletion context could still reveal a phenotype outside this basal assay.
summary: 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA had 61 Camta1-perturbed cells, a flat Camta1 self row, 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes, and no near-threshold recurrent core gene.
why_it_matters: Unlike 009, 012, and 046, the LGE/LSX group did not even show Snhg11 or Snrpn approaching FDR significance, supporting a genuine basal no-effect in this lineage and stage.

literature_claim: Mouse studies found broad synaptic Caskin1 expression and mild single-knockout behavior, while stronger spine, LTP, and memory phenotypes were revealed by combined Caskin1/Caskin2 loss.
main_caveats: A structural, electrophysiologic, or double-Caskin phenotype could occur without a nuclear RNA signature; DNA indel burden was not measured.
summary: 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut and 155 MB Glut had significant Caskin1 self-RNA decreases but no downstream genes at FDR<0.10.
why_it_matters: These are the strongest nulls because the target transcript itself moved; their flat downstream surface points to buffered scaffold biology, not to a simple lack of Caskin1 RNA knockdown.

why_it_matters: The hippocampal and cortical synaptic literature predicts effects on spines, AMPAR phosphorylation, and learning after germline double-Caskin loss, not necessarily a basal RNA response after sparse P16 single-gene loss.

literature_claim: Caskin1 protein is broadly distributed in mouse brain and spinal cord, but reported knockout phenotypes are behavioral and synaptic-structural rather than group-specific RNA phenotypes in these nuclei classes.

why_it_matters: Literature establishes broad neuronal Caskin1 protein but gives weaker reasons to expect an acute cell-autonomous RNA program in these specific groups; the likely missing phenotypes are synaptic protein architecture, phosphorylation, behavior, or unsampled spinal circuitry rather than basal nuclear transcription.

main_caveats: DNA editing was not assayed; however, the flat Casr self-transcript is expected for sparse CRISPR indel screens and is not by itself a failed-perturbation call.
summary: Twenty recovered Casr cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite 31-208 perturbed nuclei per group and Casr self FDR=1.0 in every group.
why_it_matters: The zeroes should not be read as evidence that CaSR is inert in brain. The literature-supported CaSR phenotypes are concentrated in parathyroid/kidney calcium homeostasis, glial or precursor differentiation, cerebellar granule-cell maturation, embryonic neurite growth, and acute synaptic physiology, whereas this experiment removed Casr after P16 in sparse postmitotic NeuN+ neurons and measured steady-state nuclear RNA.

why_it_matters: The expected Casz1 biology is a progenitor, retinal, cardiac, vascular, or tumor program, whereas this experiment edited already specified NeuN+ brain neurons at P16 and harvested 3-4 weeks later; the zero therefore should not be read as a failed KO or as evidence that Casz1 is inert in its developmental compartments.

literature_claim: Cbl-b loss is predicted to de-repress immune receptor and tyrosine-kinase signaling, while neuronal Cbl/Cbl-b phenotypes have been observed mainly in dual-depletion, ligand, or apoptotic-stress paradigms.
main_caveats: The assignment is mechanistic and context-based; complete DNA editing and single-cell protein loss were not measured.

why_it_matters: The expected strong biology for Cbl-b loss is TCR/NK/myeloid activation, Cbl-family growth-factor tuning, or stress-evoked JNK control; those effects would either occur in lineages removed by NeuN sorting or require Cbl co-depletion, ligand/deprivation contexts, and protein/phosphoprotein readouts. The basal mTOR/ERK secondary transcriptomes that this snRNA assay could have detected were seen after Tsc2 or Map2k1/Ntrk2 perturbation but not after Cblb.

literature_claim: CCDC50-V2/Ccdc50-Vx3 promoted axonal and dendritic outgrowth and induced NGFR-JNK/c-Jun signaling in early cultured mouse, rat, and SH-SY5Y neuronal systems.
main_caveats: Primary morphology was not measured; EGFR and c-Jun were not perturbation targets; the Ccdc50 transcript itself showed only weak uncorrected drops, and indel engagement is unknown.
summary: Ccdc50 produced zero downstream FDR<0.10 genes across the measured cortical and hippocampal glutamatergic classes.
why_it_matters: The neuron-intrinsic prior from CCDC50-V2 is an early axon/dendrite-outgrowth program with MAP2/TUBB3 and NGFR-JNK/c-Jun readouts; CRISPR here began at P16, after these excitatory classes were born and specified, so the null is more likely a developmental-window miss than proof that Ccdc50 is irrelevant to early neurite construction.

literature_claim: CCDC50 suppresses inducible NF-κB, interferon, inflammasome, lysophagy, and aggrephagy pathways by binding ubiquitinated cargoes; these pathways predict a detectable secondary stress/innate RNA program only when the relevant stimulus or cargo is present.
main_caveats: A viral, STING, NLRP3, lysosome-damage, or proteotoxic challenge could reveal effects absent at baseline; the screen did not assay autophagic flux or cargo proteins.
summary: Ccdc50 was also null in 13 GABAergic, thalamic, hypothalamic, midbrain, pontine/medullary, pineal, and cerebellar neuronal groups.
why_it_matters: The dominant later CCDC50 mechanisms are selective removal of stress- or pathogen-generated K63-ubiquitinated substrates, ruptured lysosomes, or aggregates. In basal young neurons, the expected secondary IFN, NF-κB, inflammasome, proteostatic, or lysosomal transcriptional cascade was absent, which is an informative contextual negative rather than a snRNA-seq readout failure.

literature_claim: Published Cck and CCK-receptor perturbations emphasize secreted GPCR signaling, germline or regional circuit manipulations, behavior, synaptic plasticity, and embryonic receptor synergy rather than a tonic P37-P44 cell-autonomous transcriptome.
main_caveats: Edited DNA and CCK peptide were not assayed; terminal gut, olfactory and hindbrain outputs were outside the sampled tissue; the 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut minimum downstream FDR was subthreshold at 0.143 and was not interpreted as a program.
summary: All 21 null groups and the weak 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut group lacked any downstream FDR<0.10 Cck response.
why_it_matters: For Cck, the missing signal is mechanistically expected: a sparse CRISPR edit removes a secreted neuropeptide from only the guide-bearing postmitotic neuron, while unedited neighbours can still supply ligand and many canonical outputs are receptor-, circuit-, gut/endocrine- or electrophysiology-level. The null is therefore strong evidence against a large basal cell-autonomous nuclear program, but weak evidence that CCK biology is absent.

literature_claim: CCKAR effects are linked to embryonic receptor synergy, restricted brain expression, CCK1R/CCK2R compensation, transient ependymal expression, and vagal-afferent CCK signaling.
main_caveats: DNA editing and protein loss were not measured; a rare Cckar+ neuronal subset could be diluted within a broad taxonomy group.
summary: Twenty-one Cckar cell groups were strict nulls: each had zero downstream genes at FDR<0.10 despite 24-223 perturbed cells, and the Cckar transcript itself was FDR=1.0.
why_it_matters: The best-developed CCKAR phenotypes are embryonic CCKAR/CCKBR cooperation, transient infant ependymal CCK1R, vagal-afferent satiety, and rapid GPCR calcium or ionic responses; those effects either occur before the P16 edit, in non-NeuN+ or peripheral/hindbrain lineages, or on a non-transcriptional ligand-evoked axis.

literature_claim: CCK1R is a ligand-gated GPCR with limited CNS distribution rather than a known regulator of these isolated Ank2 or cerebellar synaptic candidate genes.
main_caveats: The two groups have plausible hypothalamic or cerebellar biology only at the nominal tail; the FDR-defined dataset contains no downstream positives.
summary: 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut and 308 CB GABA had the only sub-threshold Cckar tails, but neither reached FDR<0.10: Ank2 FDR=0.143 in 110, and Efr3b/Sh2d5/Unc5c each FDR=0.115 in 308.
why_it_matters: Weak, isolated nominal genes are less convincing than the strict nulls and do not support Ank2, Efr3b, Sh2d5, or Unc5c as CCKAR biomarkers without a stronger perturbation or a ligand-evoked assay in a purified CCK1R-responsive population.

why_it_matters: The negative surface is not best read as failed editing. CCK receptor developmental transcription requires embryonic timing and Cckar+Cckbr co-loss, whereas adult CCK2R biology is ligand-, circuit-, and second-messenger-dependent; a P16 single-receptor mosaic LoF in resting NeuN-positive nuclei is therefore displaced from the contexts where a response is expected.

main_caveats: No DNA indel measurements are available, and sparse snRNA-seq cannot exclude acute calcium, migration, or ligand-binding defects in Ccr2-expressing immune cells that were not sampled.
summary: All 22 Ccr2-recovered NeuN+ neuronal cell groups had 0 downstream FDR<0.10 genes; the single missing group, 215 MB Dopa, was not tested for Ccr2 rather than scored as zero.
why_it_matters: CCR2 loss is expected to alter CCL2-driven monocyte/macrophage recruitment and neuroinflammatory infiltration, not the resting transcriptome of sparse mature neurons; the absent CCL2-ligand, NFκB, STAT3, IL-1β, and interferon-marker rows show that a detectable inflammatory feedback program never fired in the sampled cells. Therefore the null is displaced to under-sampled myeloid/vascular lineages and to injury or ligand-rich contexts, not to a generic lack of CRISPR efficacy.

literature_claim: CCSER1/FAM190A loss perturbs cytokinesis in dividing cells and overexpression perturbs centrosome and mitotic programs in cancer models.
main_caveats: DNA indel engagement was not assayed, but flat self-transcript FDRs are expected in this CRISPR format and are not by themselves grounds to call failed targeting.
summary: All 21 measured Ccser1 cell groups had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10; 046 CTX-CGE GABA was only subthreshold, with minimum downstream FDR 0.191, and the two dopaminergic/pineal groups had no Ccser1 rows and were not tested.
why_it_matters: Published perturbation phenotypes place CCSER1 at mitotic spindle and cytokinetic structures in cycling cells, whereas this experiment perturbed NeuN-enriched postmitotic neurons at P16. The zero is therefore poor evidence that Ccser1 is biologically irrelevant, but good evidence that acute postnatal neuronal loss does not trigger a secondary stress, UPR, proteostatic, or synaptic transcriptome detectable at FDR<0.10.

why_it_matters: Given CD14's GPI-anchored LPS/TLR co-receptor role in macrophages and microglia, the real effect is expected in non-neuronal innate immune lineages and inflammatory ligand contexts absent from this NeuN-enriched postnatal screen; the null should therefore not be read as global Cd14 inactivity.

main_caveats: RGCs, T cells, DNA indels, CD3-zeta protein, phospho-Syk/ZAP70, receptor localization, and synaptic physiology were not measured; 215 MB Dopa had no Cd247 rows and is not part of this null.

why_it_matters: The null is not a generic low-knockdown failure call. Canonical Cd247 biology is T-cell ITAM signaling in a lineage removed by NeuN+ sorting, the best retinal phenotype is outside the sampled tissue, the EphA4/ZAP70/Syk phenotype acts before neurite outgrowth, and the hippocampal and retinal synaptic phenotypes are dominated by receptor localization or electrophysiology rather than by a required whole-nucleus mRNA cascade.

why_it_matters: The canonical CD27-CD70/TRAF/NF-kB/JNK signal belongs to activated lymphocyte/APC biology, whereas the assay sampled NeuN+ postmitotic neuronal nuclei. The expected secondary NF-kB/JNK/survival mRNAs were absent, so the null is informative for sampled neurons but should flip in the appropriate immune lineage.

why_it_matters: Known high-effect CD2AP biology lies in podocyte slit-diaphragm survival, immune-cell scaffolding, microglia, endothelial barrier function, and local neuronal F-actin/endosomal/synaptic protein turnover. A NeuN-enriched P16-to-P37/44 snRNA assay would detect a secondary nuclear stress, lysosomal, or APP-processing mRNA response if one were large, but it is not the primary assay for spine morphology, APP/BACE1 colocalization, vesicle recycling, proteasome flux, blood-brain-barrier leakage, or microgliosis.

why_it_matters: The literature-obvious CD36 programs require microglial, macrophage, endothelial or vascular cells and ligands such as beta-amyloid or oxidized lipid; those lineages and challenges are absent from this sparse NeuN+ juvenile screen, so the zeros place CD36 action off-axis rather than proving that CD36 is globally inert in brain.

why_it_matters: VMH CD36 is expected to alter oleic-acid-evoked calcium or membrane-potential responses in a restricted metabolic-sensing circuit; a pooled resting snRNA-seq group can miss that evoked physiology and can dilute ARC/VMN peptide and fatty-acid genes that were FDR=1.0 here.

literature_claim: Cd3d is part of the TCR/CD3 complex and is required in thymic T-cell selection rather than in postmitotic brain neurons.

summary: Cd3d had 0 downstream genes at FDR<0.10 in every one of the 21 measured neuronal cell groups; the two groups 215 MB Dopa and 217 P MY Pineal Glut had no Cd3d rows and were not tested.
why_it_matters: The expected loss-of-function phenotype is defective TCR/CD3 assembly and thymocyte signaling in the T-cell lineage, which was absent from this NeuN-enriched brain-nucleus readout. Thus the null is strong for the sampled postmitotic neurons but would be expected to flip in thymocytes or T cells.
